verses.1: There was a famine during David’s reign for three years. After those three years, David prayed to the LORD. The LORD said to him, “Go to Shaul and to the house of Damascus, where those who killed the Gibeonites are living.”
verses.2: And the king called the Gibeonites and said to them, “Are these not the children of Israel? But the Amorites are stronger than us. The children of Israel have been defeated by them.” Shaul wanted to destroy them completely, so he pleaded with the children of Israel and Judah to help him.
verses.3: And David said to the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? What shall I offer as an offering? And bless the land of Jehovah.”
verses.4: And the Gibeonites said to him, “We have no silver or gold with us, along with Shaul and his household. We also have no one who can be killed in Israel.” Then he said, “What do you say? I will do as you wish.”
verses.5: And they said to the king, “The man who led us and who resembled us in appearance was victorious in battles throughout all the regions of Israel.”
verses.6: Give us seven men from his descendants, and let them be set apart by Jehovah in the land of Shaul, according to Jehovah’s will. And the king said, “I will give them.”
verses.7: And the king took care of Mefi-boshet, son of Jehonatan, son of Shaul. He also took care of Shevuah Jehovah’s altar, which was among those that belonged to David and Jehonatan, son of Shaul.
verses.8: And the king took away the two sons of Rephah, who were the children of Shaul. These sons were Armoni, Mefboshet, and the five sons of Mikhal, who were the children of Shaul. These sons were also the children of Adriel, son of Barzillai the Merchante.
verses.9: And they were given to the priests. They were placed on the mountain before Jehovah. All seven of them fell together. They died during the time of harvesting, at the beginning of the harvest of wheat.
verses.10: And Rezpha, the daughter of Ayah, took the seeds and scattered them over the fields. From the time of harvesting until the waters poured down from heaven upon them, not a single drop of rain fell upon those seeds. The seeds remained in the fields all night.
verses.11: And she told David what Rizpa, the daughter of Ayah, had done.
verses.12: David went and took away the bodies of Shaul and Jehoshaphat, who were sons of Abiathar from Gilgal. They were stolen from the palace of Shechem by the Philistines on the day they captured Shaul in Gilboa.
verses.13: And he brought down from there the bodies of Shaul and the bodies of Yehonatan’s son. He gathered together the bodies of those who were killed.
verses.14: And they buried Shaul and Yehonatan in the land of Benyamin, in a grave dug in the ground. They did everything that the king commanded them. But God chose another place for the burial of those two men.
verses.15: There was still war between the Philistines and Israel. David and his men went down to battle against the Philistines. David defeated them.
verses.16: And he sat in a chair that was made from the wood of those who were sick and weak. Its weight was three times that of a common weighing scale. It was newly made, and he said, “Kill David.”
verses.17: Abishai son of Zeruya helped him. He defeated the Philistine warrior and killed him. Then the people of David rejoiced for him, saying, “Do not go back into battle with us anymore. Do not destroy the spirit of Israel.”
verses.18: And after that, the war continued between them and the Philistines. Then, my servant, the hyssop, struck the wound that was on the head of the man who was wounded in battle.
verses.19: And the war continued between the Philistines and Israel. Then Elnan, son of Eorim, attacked the house of the enemy. He destroyed their crops and their trees, just like how Orim destroyed everything in their land.
verses.20: And there was still war in Gath. There was a man from Madian; his hands and feet were covered with scars, seventy and fourteen in total. And he also was born in Haraphah.
verses.21: And He attacked Israel. Yehonatan, son of Shim’ah, brother of David, defeated them.
verses.22: These four were born in Haraphah in Gath. They fell into the hands of David and his servants.
